instruction: Read all paper titles from the opened references.docx and write them into references.bib (one title per line). The docx is already open in LibreOffice Writer.

titles: Spider: A Large-Scale Human-Labeled Dataset for Complex and Cross-Domain Semantic Parsing and Text-to-SQL Task
SParC: Cross-Domain Semantic Parsing in Context
CoSQL: A Conversational Text-to-SQL Challenge Towards Cross-Domain Natural Language Interfaces to Databases
BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to export DBLP BibTeX for 6 papers. Searched for 'Spider' on DBLP successfully, found results. Then opened terminal, tried curl API requests and wrote a Python script to automate BibTeX fetching. Got stuck automating and ran out of 50 turns without completing.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can search papers on DBLP, navigate Chrome, open terminal, run curl/pip commands, write Python scripts, switch between applications, read docx content
metadata.failure_analysis: Task too complex (6 papers). Model attempted to automate via Python script instead of manually fetching each BibTeX entry. Script writing consumed most turns without producing correct output.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to just copying paper titles from docx to bib file. Removes the DBLP lookup complexity while testing cross-app text transfer capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires reading 6 paper titles from references.docx in LibreOffice Writer and writing them into references.bib. Evaluator checks bib file contains all 6 titles with partial credit (1/6 per title). Postconfig saves the file before evaluation.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads references.bib file content via env.controller.get_file() and returns it in a dict with 'content' key
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('titles', []) without wrapping in 'rules' key
All 6 paper titles from the instruction are checked with partial credit scoring (1/6 per title), providing complete coverage
Fuzzy keyword matching (70% of words >3 chars) is a reasonable approach that tolerates minor formatting differences while still verifying title presence
Postconfig correctly activates the bib file window and saves with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring file content is written to disk
Data flow is correct: getter returns {'content': str} -> metric reads result.get('content', '').lower() for case-insensitive comparison
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Cannot independently verify that the 6 expected titles exactly match the actual content of references.docx (the downloaded file). If the docx contains different or additional titles, the evaluator would not catch missing ones.

Minor: The postconfig saves via Ctrl+S in the active window (references.bib in VS Code). If the agent wrote to the file via terminal/script rather than VS Code, the Ctrl+S would save an empty buffer. However, the getter reads the file from disk directly, so this is only a concern if the agent edited in VS Code without saving - the postconfig handles that case well.
